items.title: Great Leap Forward

edges.quote: The effects on the upper levels of government in response to the disaster were complex, with Mao purging the Minister of National Defense Peng Dehuai in 1959, the temporary promotion of Lin Biao, Liu Shaoqi, and Deng Xiaoping, and Mao losing some power and prestige following the Great Leap Forward, during the Seven Thousand Cadres Conference in 1962, which led him to launch the Cultural Revolution in 1966.
edges.explanation: The article "Great Leap Forward" (revision 1379962036) states: "The effects on the upper levels of government in response to the disaster were complex, with Mao purging the Minister of National Defense Peng Dehuai in 1959, the temporary promotion of Lin Biao, Liu Shaoqi, and Deng Xiaoping, and Mao losing some power and prestige following the Great Leap Forward, during the Seven Thousand Cadres Conference in 1962, which led him to launch the Cultural Revolution in 1966." What the sentence says led Mao to launch the Cultural Revolution is the power and prestige he lost following the Great Leap Forward, which is this record's own consequence.

items.why: Asia trails. A level 4 vital article, and its own article states what the loss of prestige after it led Mao to launch. Its one class, campaign, has no row in the class table yet.

items.title: Reform and opening up

edges.quote: A longer-run result was that there were not nearly as many well-entrenched interest groups as in the Soviet Union and the Eastern Bloc, so when Deng Xiaoping and the other pragmatists took power, few interest groups remained whose lobbying could undermine Deng's market-oriented reforms, because the Cultural Revolution had destroyed the narrowly entrenched interests with a stake in the status quo.
edges.explanation: The article "Reform and opening up" (revision 1373006392) states: "A longer-run result was that there were not nearly as many well-entrenched interest groups as in the Soviet Union and the Eastern Bloc, so when Deng Xiaoping and the other pragmatists took power, few interest groups remained whose lobbying could undermine Deng's market-oriented reforms, because the Cultural Revolution had destroyed the narrowly entrenched interests with a stake in the status quo." The sentence gives the Cultural Revolution as what left these reforms without organised opposition, so the edge runs from the Cultural Revolution and the type is enabled.

items.why: Asia trails. A level 4 vital article, and its own article names what left these reforms without organised opposition. Its classes have no row in the class table yet.

items.title: 1970 Bhola cyclone

edges.quote: The poor and discriminatory response from the West Pakistan government led to the increasingly widespread disillusionment from the East Pakistani people, allowing the opposition Awami League to gain a landslide victory in the province during the election that took place a month later as well as the Bangladesh Liberation War seven months later.
edges.explanation: The article "1970 Bhola cyclone" (revision 1378967090) states: "The poor and discriminatory response from the West Pakistan government led to the increasingly widespread disillusionment from the East Pakistani people, allowing the opposition Awami League to gain a landslide victory in the province during the election that took place a month later as well as the Bangladesh Liberation War seven months later." The response the sentence names is the response to this cyclone, in the cyclone's own article. The type is enabled and not caused, because the sentence says the disillusionment allowed the war.

items.why: Asia trails. A level 4 vital article, the deadliest tropical cyclone recorded, and its own article states what the response to it allowed. Its one class, tropical cyclone, has no row in the class table yet.

items.title: Decolonisation of Africa

edges.quote: Italy, a colonial power, lost its African empire, Italian East Africa, Italian Ethiopia, Italian Eritrea, Italian Somalia and Italian Libya, as a result of World War II.
edges.explanation: The article "Decolonisation of Africa" (revision 1379719162) states: "Italy, a colonial power, lost its African empire, Italian East Africa, Italian Ethiopia, Italian Eritrea, Italian Somalia and Italian Libya, as a result of World War II." The loss it names is part of what this record is: the edge reads that sentence and nothing more, and the scope the sentence gives it is Italy's empire.

items.why: Writer A logged this item skipped on 12 October, because the old reading of --held counted a record on m0 as held by the other branch. M91 change 6 fixed that and the edge was never written, so it comes back under a new id.

items.title: Scramble for Africa

edges.quote: After the Independence of Brazil in 1822, Portugal sought to protect, develop and expand its remaining overseas territories in order to compensate for the loss of Brazilian trade and revenue and its international standing, leading to an aggressive expansion of its Angolan and Mozambican territories.
edges.explanation: The article "Scramble for Africa" (revision 1376647971) states: "After the Independence of Brazil in 1822, Portugal sought to protect, develop and expand its remaining overseas territories in order to compensate for the loss of Brazilian trade and revenue and its international standing, leading to an aggressive expansion of its Angolan and Mozambican territories." The expansion it names is Portugal's share of the scramble, which is what this record holds; the edge reads that sentence and nothing more.

edges.quote: The tensions between the imperial powers led to a succession of crises, which exploded in August 1914, when previous rivalries and alliances created a domino situation that drew the major European nations into World War I.
edges.explanation: The article "Scramble for Africa" (revision 1376647971) states: "The tensions between the imperial powers led to a succession of crises, which exploded in August 1914, when previous rivalries and alliances created a domino situation that drew the major European nations into World War I." The tensions are the scramble's own, in the scramble's own article; precondition-of and not caused, because the sentence makes the rivalry what the crises grew out of.

items.why: Skipped on 12 October for the same reason as the item above. Two edges, neither of them written, so it comes back under a new id.

items.title: 12-3 incident

edges.quote: Portuguese sovereignty over Macau severely diminished after the incident, leading to de facto Chinese suzerainty over the territory 33 years prior to the eventual handover of Macau.
edges.explanation: The article "12-3 incident" (revision 1377636747) states: "Portuguese sovereignty over Macau severely diminished after the incident, leading to de facto Chinese suzerainty over the territory 33 years prior to the eventual handover of Macau." The sentence dates the end of effective Portuguese rule to the incident and the handover 33 years after it, which is a precondition and not a cause.

items.why: Skipped on 12 October for the same reason as the two items above. The edge was never written, so it comes back under a new id.
